declarations.doc: Invariant: product of reserves is non-decreasing after a fee-bearing swap.
declarations.name: cpProduct

declarations.doc:
Healthy iff collateralValue * ltvBps >= debtValue * 10000.
Prices are abstract positive integers; values = amount * price.
declarations.name: collValue

declarations.doc: Shares minted for a deposit of `assets` into a pool with totals.
declarations.name: sharesFromAssets

declarations.doc: Assets redeemed for burning `shares`.
declarations.name: assetsFromShares

declarations.doc: CPAMM first deposit: geometric mean of amounts (Uni V2: sqrt(a0*a1) - MINIMUM).
declarations.name: geometricMint

declarations.doc:
Accrue index by simple interest: index' = index * (BASE + rateBps * dt) / BASE
rateBps is basis points per time unit (abstract).
declarations.name: accrueIndex

declarations.doc: Seized collateral for a repayment at liquidation incentive (bps, e.g. 10500 = 5% bonus).
declarations.name: seizeCollateral

declarations.doc: Two-slope kinked borrow rate (Aave-style), returns rate in bps.
declarations.name: twoSlopeRate

declarations.doc:
Output amount for a constant-product swap with fee taken from input.
feeNum/feeDen: e.g. Uni V2 uses 997/1000 (0.3% fee).
declarations.name: cpAmountOut

declarations.doc: Post-swap reserves (input token grows, output shrinks).
declarations.name: cpApplySwap

declarations.doc:
AUTHORITY principals (6h).  `gov` holds feeToSetter at genesis; `mallory`
never can, absent a handover from `gov`.  Two principals — one in the role
and one out — is what hosts the permission witnesses.
declarations.name: GOV

declarations.doc:
AUTHORITY (6h).  UniswapV2Factory.sol:40,45 — both `setFeeTo` and
`setFeeToSetter` require `msg.sender == feeToSetter`, so the role is a
closed cycle: no account outside it can ever enter.  A `var`, not a
constant, because :45 lets the holder pass it on.
declarations.name: feeToSetter

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.sol:99 — denominator = rootK*5 + rootKLast
declarations.name: FEE_MINT_SHARE

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.sol:74, descaled from uint112(-1).  See BOUNDS.
declarations.name: MAX_RESERVE

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.sol:121 — address(0), holder of the permanent lock.
declarations.name: LOCK

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Factory.sol:7 — feeTo, holder of the protocol cut.
declarations.name: PROTOCOL_FEE_TO

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.sol:15
declarations.name: MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.sol:180-181 — balanceAdjusted = balance*1000 - amountIn*3
declarations.name: FEE_NUM

declarations.doc:
CONSERVATION — LP shares are neither created nor destroyed outside mint,
burn and the protocol cut.  This is the T2 command's invariant.
PERMISSION-DEPENDENCE: same reserves, same switch, different holder,
different enablement.
declarations.name: maySetFee

declarations.doc:
NON-SURJECTIVE (SURJECTIVITY.md): `mallory` reaches the role only by a
handover from `gov` — never by any action of its own.  Must be [violation].
declarations.name: wit_feeAuthorityHandedOver

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Pair.sol:121 — the lock is permanent.  It is minted once, at the
bootstrap, to an account with no burn path, so once the pool exists the
supply can never fall below it.
declarations.name: inv_permanentLock

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Pair.sol:28 — kLast is the product AT THE LAST LIQUIDITY EVENT,
and swaps only raise the product (that is what the 997/1000 buys), so a
live kLast never exceeds the current product.  This is the invariant that
v1 could not even state, because nothing in v1 read kLast.
declarations.name: inv_kLastMeaning

declarations.doc:
LP supply never exceeds the geometric mean of the reserves.  Tight at the
bootstrap (equality), and preserved by every action including the protocol
cut, whose 1/6-of-growth form is chosen precisely so it cannot break this.
declarations.name: inv_supplyBelowGeometric

declarations.doc:
T0-LIVE for this protocol: geometricMint(4000, 9000) = 5000, as a TRACE.
Under M1 (v1's min) the same trace gives totalSupply 5000 and minter LP
3000, so this state is unreachable and the witness is never violated —
which is exactly how a value-level equality is turned into a mechanism
check.  Reached at depth 1 from init.
declarations.name: wit_live_geometricMint

declarations.doc:
`proportionalMint` ran: two distinct LPs hold shares, and only one of them
can have taken the bootstrap branch.  Also discharges regression signal 7
(single-user-sufficient invariants).
declarations.name: wit_used_proportionalMint

declarations.doc:
`proportionalBurn` ran: every non-locked share has been redeemed and the
pool still holds reserves against the 1000 that can never come out.
declarations.name: wit_used_proportionalBurn

declarations.doc:
`mintFeeLiquidity` ran and PAID: feeTo holds shares.  No other writer
exists for that account.  This is the witness v1 could not host at all.
declarations.name: wit_used_mintFeeLiquidity

declarations.doc:
`ammAmountOut` (and with it `kGuardHolds`) ran: the product has risen above
its value at the last liquidity event, which only a swap can do.  This is
kLast being read as an observable, not merely written.
declarations.name: wit_used_ammAmountOut

declarations.doc:
The pool exists, governance has switched the cut off, and the next
liquidity event has zeroed kLast.  Under v1 this branch does not exist.
declarations.name: wit_branch_feeOff

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Factory.setFeeTo (:40-43).  Governance flips the switch; kLast is
NOT touched here.  The teardown at UniswapV2Pair.sol:104-106 happens on the
next liquidity event, which is where `kLast' = if (feeOn) ... else 0` sits.
declarations.name: setFeeTo

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Factory.sol:45 `setFeeToSetter` — the handover, and the reason
`feeToSetter` is state rather than a constant.  Authority over the
authority: the holder alone decides who holds it next.
declarations.name: setFeeToSetter

declarations.doc:
T3 for this protocol (P2-SCOPE §5 row 1): `isqrtFloor` is the exact floor
at every product this run actually reaches.  False for any inexact rival.
declarations.name: inv_sqrtExact

declarations.doc:
`isqrtFloor` ran and its TRUNCATION was load-bearing: a state whose supply
is the strict floor of sqrt(k).  Reached at (1000, 2000): 1414^2 < 2e6.
declarations.name: wit_used_isqrtFloor

declarations.doc:
`geometricMint` ran OFF THE DIAGONAL — the region where every member of
𝔐 disagrees with M0.  A diagonal-only witness would prove nothing, which
is precisely v1's defect.
declarations.name: wit_used_geometricMint

declarations.doc:
FIRST DEPOSIT — UniswapV2Pair.sol:120
  liquidity = Math.sqrt(amount0.mul(amount1)).sub(MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY)
The geometric mean is the unique symmetric degree-1-homogeneous function
whose level sets are the constant-product curve, so "shares == the
invariant" IS the mechanism.  A negative result is `SafeMath.sub`
reverting; the caller's `liq > 0` guard is exactly that refusal.
declarations.name: geometricMint

declarations.doc:
LATER DEPOSITS — UniswapV2Pair.sol:123
  Math.min(amount0.mul(_totalSupply)/_reserve0,
           amount1.mul(_totalSupply)/_reserve1)
Both quotients floor: the pool keeps the residual, not the depositor.
declarations.name: proportionalMint

declarations.doc:
EXIT — UniswapV2Pair.sol:144-145
  amountX = liquidity.mul(balanceX) / _totalSupply
Floors again: the residual stays with the remaining LPs.
declarations.name: proportionalBurn

declarations.doc:
EXACT FILL against the pair's own admissibility test.  The pair does not
compute an output; it accepts any (in, out) satisfying the K guard at
:180-182.  This is the largest such `out`, which is what a router sends.
The 997/1000 is why k strictly grows and why LPs are paid at all.
declarations.name: ammAmountOut

declarations.doc:
THE PAIR'S OWN GUARD — UniswapV2Pair.sol:180-182, verbatim:
  balance0Adjusted = balance0.mul(1000).sub(amount0In.mul(3))
  balance1Adjusted = balance1.mul(1000).sub(amount1In.mul(3))
  require(balance0Adjusted.mul(balance1Adjusted)
          >= uint(_reserve0).mul(_reserve1).mul(1000**2), 'UniswapV2: K')
Peak intermediate: (MAX_RESERVE*FEE_DEN)^2 = 1.0e16.
declarations.name: kGuardHolds

declarations.doc:
PROTOCOL CUT — UniswapV2Pair.sol:92-103.  Reads kLast, which is what makes
kLast live; v1 wrote kLast at three sites and had no reader at all.
  rootK > rootKLast  =>  totalSupply*(rootK - rootKLast)
                         / (rootK*5 + rootKLast)
Caller supplies the feeOn gate (:93).  kLast == 0 is the first-ever
liquidity event (:94), which mints nothing.
declarations.name: mintFeeLiquidity

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Pair.swap (:159-187), token0 in.  The pair transfers out first
and then checks the K guard on the resulting balances (:180-182).
declarations.name: swap0for1

declarations.doc: UniswapV2Pair.swap (:159-187), token1 in.
declarations.name: swap1for0

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Pair.mint (:110-131).  _mintFee runs FIRST (:117), against the
pre-update reserves and the pre-mint totalSupply, and its result changes
the denominator of the pro-rata branch (:118 exists for exactly that).
declarations.name: mint

declarations.doc:
UniswapV2Pair.burn (:134-156).  `shares` is the LP the caller transferred
to the pair before the call; the guard below is (E<=) on that transfer.
declarations.name: burn

declarations.doc:
Convention 6: every `nondet` is exogenous — a caller identity, a token
amount the caller transferred, or the factory's governance switch.  The
protocol selects nothing here that the driver could be told.
declarations.name: step

declarations.doc:
Exact floor(sqrt(n)) for 0 <= n < 4^bits.
`bits` fold steps; each step is one multiply and one compare.
Largest intermediate is (2^bits)^2 = 4^bits, so pick `bits` so that
4^bits fits the backend integer width (Rust backend: bits <= 31).
declarations.name: isqrtBits

declarations.doc: TypeScript backend (BigInt): exact on 0 <= n < 2^128.
declarations.name: isqrtWide

declarations.doc: Defining property of floor(sqrt).
declarations.name: isqrtCorrect

declarations.doc: Quint Rust-backend integer ceiling.  Every `BOUNDS:` peak must be below it.
declarations.name: I64_MAX

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:76 specialised to the 2-coin pool (P2-SCOPE row 2
permits the 3 -> 2 reduction).
declarations.name: NEWTON_N

declarations.doc: Unrolling depth of the `for _i in range(255)` loop.  See the note above.
declarations.name: NEWTON_K

declarations.doc:
The loop carriage: the current iterate, the previous one (the contract's
`Dprev`), whether the contract's `break` has fired, and the real iteration
count.  `v`/`vprev` are read by `newtonBreak`, `done` and `iters` by
`kernelNewtonOk` and by every caller's convergence obligation.
declarations.name: NewtonState

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:211-217, verbatim, including the branch on direction:
  if D > Dprev:  if D - Dprev <= 1: break
  else:          if Dprev - D <= 1: break
declarations.name: newtonBreak

declarations.doc: Signed magnitude.  Needed by every spec that carries a signed position.
declarations.name: absInt

declarations.doc:
`isqrtFloor` — exact floor(sqrt(n)) on 0 <= n < 2^62, 31 restoring folds.
Verified at gate 2.0d on ~14k points; see `kernelSqrtVerified`.
Peak intermediate inside the fold: (2^31 - 1)^2 = 4.611686e18 < I64_MAX.
Models `Math.sqrt` (Uniswap_v2-core/contracts/libraries/Math.sol:11-20),
whose Babylonian loop returns the same exact floor for every uint.
declarations.name: isqrtFloor

declarations.doc: The defining property of floor(sqrt), for use in `inv_sqrtExact`.
declarations.name: isqrtExactAt

declarations.doc:
Take one step to `vNew` and evaluate the contract's break condition on the
pair (new, previous).  Every Newton loop in the corpus goes through here.
declarations.name: newtonAdvance

declarations.doc:
One iteration of StableSwap3Pool.vy:206-210, same rounding, same order:
  D_P = D*D/(x*N) ; D_P = D_P*D/(y*N)
  D   = (Ann*S + D_P*N)*D / ((Ann-1)*D + (N+1)*D_P)
Once `done` the accumulator is the identity, which is what `break` means.
declarations.name: newtonDStep

declarations.doc:
StableSwap3Pool.vy:195-218 for N = 2, unrolled to `maxIter`.
`S == 0` returns 0 (:199-200); a zero balance is the contract's own
division-by-zero case (:208 comment, "only withdrawal will work"), so it is
returned as 0 with the loop never entered.
declarations.name: newtonDFull

declarations.doc: The value the contract returns.  Callers MUST also assert `newtonDConverged`.
declarations.name: newtonD

declarations.doc:
The proof obligation the unrolling exports: the loop terminated the way the
contract's `break` would.  False means K is too small AT THIS POINT and the
returned D is not the contract's D.
declarations.name: newtonDConverged

declarations.doc: The real iteration count, i.e. how many times the contract's loop body ran.
declarations.name: newtonDIters

declarations.doc:
|D_next - D| at the returned D: the residual of the fixpoint equation the
iteration solves.  `<= 1` is the contract's own tolerance (:211-217).
declarations.name: newtonDResidual
kernelNewtonOk

550.doc:
PROTOCOL CUT — UniswapV2Pair.sol:92-103.  Reads kLast, which is what makes
kLast live; v1 wrote kLast at three sites and had no reader at all.
  rootK > rootKLast  =>  totalSupply*(rootK - rootKLast)
                         / (rootK*5 + rootKLast)
Caller supplies the feeOn gate (:93).  kLast == 0 is the first-ever
liquidity event (:94), which mints nothing.
550.name: mintFeeLiquidity

565.doc:
FIRST DEPOSIT — UniswapV2Pair.sol:120
  liquidity = Math.sqrt(amount0.mul(amount1)).sub(MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY)
The geometric mean is the unique symmetric degree-1-homogeneous function
whose level sets are the constant-product curve, so "shares == the
invariant" IS the mechanism.  A negative result is `SafeMath.sub`
reverting; the caller's `liq > 0` guard is exactly that refusal.
565.name: geometricMint

571.doc:
LATER DEPOSITS — UniswapV2Pair.sol:123
  Math.min(amount0.mul(_totalSupply)/_reserve0,
           amount1.mul(_totalSupply)/_reserve1)
Both quotients floor: the pool keeps the residual, not the depositor.
571.name: proportionalMint

T0-LIVE for this protocol: geometricMint(4000, 9000) = 5000, as a TRACE.
Under M1 (v1's min) the same trace gives totalSupply 5000 and minter LP

which is exactly how a value-level equality is turned into a mechanism
check.  Reached at depth 1 from init.

`isqrtFloor` — exact floor(sqrt(n)) on 0 <= n < 2^62, 31 restoring folds.
Verified at gate 2.0d on ~14k points; see `kernelSqrtVerified`.
Peak intermediate inside the fold: (2^31 - 1)^2 = 4.611686e18 < I64_MAX.
Models `Math.sqrt` (Uniswap_v2-core/contracts/libraries/Math.sol:11-20),
whose Babylonian loop returns the same exact floor for every uint.
1223.name: isqrtFloor

1973.doc:
Exact floor(sqrt(n)) for 0 <= n < 4^bits.
`bits` fold steps; each step is one multiply and one compare.
Largest intermediate is (2^bits)^2 = 4^bits, so pick `bits` so that
4^bits fits the backend integer width (Rust backend: bits <= 31).
